Entertainment is a major part of the pitch. The glasses will be the first VR device certified as IMAX Enhanced and will support 3D movies through services including Disney+. The Facebook creator is also taking aim at live sports, saying users will have access to more than 100 immersive sporting events annually through partners including MLB, NBC Sports, TNT Sports, and UFC.

For work, the glasses can create multiple virtual screens and turn a flat surface into a keyboard and touchpad. Perhaps the more futuristic feature is hologram calling, which creates a digital version of the user that responds to their expressions in real time.

Arriving in Spring 2027, the glasses look like oversized sunglasses and will be paired with an external power and computing pod, similar to Apple's (AAPL) Vision Pro. At around $1,300, the glasses are hardly inexpensive, but they remain well below the Vision Pro's original $3,500 price and its current $3,700 price, making it quite an attractive deal.

About Meta Stock

Based in Menlo Park, California, Meta Platforms connects people through social media, messaging, AI, virtual and augmented reality, and wearable devices. Its Family of Apps includes Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp, Threads, and Meta AI, while Reality Labs develops Quest headsets, AI glasses, and related technologies.

That diversification has made Meta one of the technology sector's largest companies, with a market cap of about $1.9 trillion. Investors have rewarded the company handsomely this year, as META stock has gained 13% in 2026 and is up 38% in just the last three months.

Story Continues

The recent momentum is especially pronounced. Over the past five trading sessions, Meta's shares have skyrocketed 12%, with the Meta Connect event serving as a major catalyst.

That enthusiasm, however, has also come with a richer valuation. META stock currently trades at 23.95 times forward-adjusted earnings and 7.46 times sales, with both multiples above their respective industry averages.

The company also returns capital to shareholders through its dividend, distributing $2.10 per share annually, resulting in a yield of 0.28%. Its next payment of $0.53 per share is scheduled for Monday, Sept. 28, for shareholders on record as of Monday, Sept. 21.

A Closer Look at Q2 Earnings

Meta reported its Q2 FY2026 results on July 29, showing a widening gap between strong top-line growth and the rising cost of its AI ambitions. Revenue reached $60.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year (YoY) and above analysts' $60.2 billion expectation.

Advertising continued to drive growth, with Family of Apps advertising revenue increasing 27% YoY to $59.4 billion. The improvement was supported by a 14% increase in ad impressions and a 12% rise in the average price per ad, showing that the social media giant continued benefiting from stronger advertising volume as well as pricing.

The revenue momentum, however, did not carry through to the bottom line. EPS declined 13.4% to $6.18, falling short of the roughly $7.22 analysts had expected. The tech giant also reported $2.40 billion in legal-proceeding charges and $1.18 billion in severance expenses linked to its May 2026 headcount reduction.

The cost pressures extended beyond those charges. Total costs and expenses jumped 55.2% YoY to $42 billion. Meanwhile, CapEx climbed to $31.1 billion as the business accelerated spending on AI infrastructure. However, this spending surge sits at the heart of Meta's growth.

The company is delivering strong revenue growth while committing increasingly large sums to AI infrastructure, with the expectation that those investments will generate stronger returns over time, and the near-term outlook reflects that balancing act.

For Q3 FY2026, Meta expects revenue between $61 billion and $64 billion. At the same time, the company has raised its 2026 capital-spending outlook to $130-145 billion, compared with its previous guidance range of $125-145 billion.

The social media giant has also increased the lower end of its full-year expense outlook to $165-169 billion to account for the legal charge. Despite the higher cost base, management continues to expect 2026 operating income to exceed 2025's.

On the other hand, analysts project Q3 FY2026 EPS to decrease 11.9% YoY to $6.39, while FY2026 EPS is expected to decline 5.9% from the previous year to $27.93. By FY2027, however, EPS is projected to rebound 23% YoY to $34.36, offering a potentially brighter earnings trajectory as the company's investments mature.

What Do Analysts Expect for META Stock?

Analyst sentiment toward META stock remains notably positive. Ivan Feinseth of Tigress Financial reiterated his "Buy" rating and raised his price target from $945 to $995. The revised target reflects his view of the company's earnings momentum, competitive positioning, and improving growth outlook as potential drivers of further stock appreciation.

Wall Street's overall rating is "Strong Buy." Among the 54 analysts covering META, 45 rate the stock a "Strong Buy," two assign a "Moderate Buy," and seven recommend "Hold."

Price targets likewise reflect expectations for further appreciation. The average price target stands at $786.74, representing a potential upside of 5%, while the Street-high target of $1,000 implies a 33% gain from current levels.

news.Title: Alphabet vs. Apple: Which Consumer AI Tech Stock Has an Edge Now?
news.Content:
Alphabet GOOGL and Apple AAPL are intensifying their push into consumer artificial intelligence (AI), but their strategies differ significantly. Apple is embedding AI deeply across its hardware ecosystem through Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, while Alphabet is integrating Gemini across Search, the Gemini app, YouTube, Chrome and its broader services ecosystem.

However, GOOGL or AAPL, which has an edge right now?

The Case for GOOGL Stock

Alphabet's open and cloud-centric approach has been driving the popularity of its applications among consumers. The company's biggest advantage is the scale at which Gemini is already reaching consumers. The Gemini app reached 950 million monthly active users, while daily active users tripled year over year. AI Mode surpassed one billion monthly active users, and management said it is generating incremental Search queries. More than 140 million users also engaged with the Gemini-powered Ask YouTube feature on the watch page in June.

Gemini is also improving Alphabet's advertising engine. The company said Gemini enhances query understanding and enables ads to address longer, more complex searches. Advertisers adopting AI-powered campaigns such as AI Max or Performance Max are seeing an average 15% increase in conversions or value at a similar return on ad spending. This provides Alphabet with a clearer near-term pathway for monetizing consumer AI usage.

Alphabet is also rapidly improving its underlying AI models. More than 9 million developers are building monthly with its models, while its APIs process roughly 22 billion tokens per minute, up from 16 billion in the previous quarter. The company is already developing Gemini 4 after introducing newer Gemini 3.5 models, highlighting the speed of its innovation cycle.

More importantly, Alphabet is converting AI adoption into revenues. In the second quarter of 2026, revenues jumped 24% year over year to $119.8 billion, while Search & Other revenues increased 17%. Google Cloud revenues surged 82% to $24.8 billion, supported by enterprise AI infrastructure and AI solutions.

The Case for AAPL Stock

Apple benefits from its massive installed device base and vertically integrated hardware-software ecosystem. The company introduced a redesigned Siri AI, built around personal context, privacy and integration across its platforms. Apple is also running AI models both on devices and through Private Cloud Compute, allowing it to differentiate through privacy-focused AI experiences.

Apple's silicon strategy is another strength. Management highlighted the Neural Engine, unified memory architecture and power-efficient Apple silicon as foundations for on-device AI. Mac is increasingly being used for local inference, agentic AI and demanding AI-development workloads. Meanwhile, iPhone users are increasingly using AI features powered by A19 and A19 Pro chips.

Apple's financial position also remains robust. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, revenues increased 16% year over year to $109.4 billion, with iPhone revenues rising 22%, Mac revenues increasing 29% and Services revenues growing 12%. Apple's installed base reached an all-time high across major product categories and geographic segments, giving the company a large audience through which it can distribute future AI capabilities.

Apple's current AI opportunity is still more closely tied to driving hardware upgrades, enhancing device experiences and expanding Services engagement. The company's initiatives to develop next-generation AI capabilities that combine on-device processing with Private Cloud Compute are expected to stimulate future device upgrades.

However, Alphabet currently appears further along in translating AI innovation into user growth and financial performance.

With 950 million Gemini app users, more than one billion AI Mode users, rapidly rising token consumption, 17% Search growth and 82% Cloud growth, Alphabet demonstrates both massive consumer reach and increasingly visible AI monetization. news.Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella on AI: 'Trust is going to be the biggest issue for us'
news.Content:
Microsoft ( MSFT ) on Friday unveiled a r evamped version of its Copilot software , combining its chat, coding, and agentic capabilities into a single package, which it calls Autopilot.

The platform is designed to serve as a kind of one-stop shop for your work needs, such as preparing a pitch document or putting together a spreadsheet, then having AI reason over the data to provide users with insights they may not see.

But to ensure it wins over customers, CEO Satya Nadella said, Microsoft will need to win users' trust.

"Trust is going to be the biggest issue for us," Nadella told Deirdre Bosa.

"Can I really trust [AI] with all of my credentials when it does autonomous activity? How do I make sure that this is something that I can feel that I'm in control of? And in the enterprise, this is everything," he said.

The new Copilot also offers two billing options: standard per-user plans for general AI work and a pay-as-you-go option for long-tail, multistep agentic work.

Nadella said the dual offerings will prove especially beneficial to users as AI model makers and providers gradually reduce customer subsidies.

"The way I think about our subscriptions [is] it's ultimately going to deliver more value every day of the week as models improve. And then on top of that, we have usage-based functionality that any user at any time can use with no limits," the CEO explained.

"And so that combination gives us, I think, the right business model to be able to both deliver broad access, deliver the [return on investment] that's expected, and most importantly, continuously be aligned with where customers will see value," he said.

Microsoft said Copilot will automatically route user prompts to the best available model from OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) and Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), though you'll also be able to manually choose models. The company said it will add additional options from other model makers in the future.

The Windows maker said that the per-seat option will have token limits that most people will never hit.

Those who need additional capabilities, however, can opt for usage-based billing.

news.Title: Should SpaceX Investors Be Worried About Competition From Amazon?
news.Content:
Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) dominates several markets in which it competes. It has the leading market share in the U.S. e-commerce industry and the global cloud computing space. It is also a notable player in video and music streaming, as well as digital advertising. Given Amazon's track record, nobody wants to compete with the company as it can be a formidable opponent. That's why Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) should at least acknowledge Amazon's push into some of the markets where it dominates. Should SpaceX investors be worried?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Targeting a $1.6 trillion market

SpaceX's most profitable business right now is providing internet connectivity via a constellation of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites. In the second quarter, the rocket company's connectivity segment recorded $4.3 billion in revenue (more than its two other businesses combined), up almost 66% from the year-ago period. And this unit had an operating income of $1.7 billion, up 79% year over year, while SpaceX's two other segments reported operating losses.

But SpaceX has barely scratched the surface, according to its own estimates. The company has calculated a $1.6 trillion addressable market in this industry. That's why Amazon is looking to compete in this market through Amazon Leo. The e-commerce giant has contracted launch services from Arianespace, a commercial space launch provider.

Amazon recently announced that it was adding six launches to its contracted commitment, bringing its total Arianespace launch commitments from 18 to 24. Arianespace has already put 100 of Amazon's satellites into orbit across three missions (Amazon has also contracted other companies).

Amazon already has about 400 satellites in orbit and plans to start providing internet connectivity this year. And the company's remaining contracted launches should significantly expand the constellation.

SpaceX vs. Amazon

Amazon is profitable and generates significant cash flow, which can allow it to continue investing in this opportunity, even if Amazon Leo operates at a loss for a long time. The rest of the business will pick up the slack. Further, Amazon isn't getting into the rocket business (not yet anyway). The company doesn't have to spend the significant initial capital required to build and test rockets.

Story Continues

Perhaps that's an advantage it has over SpaceX. But SpaceX's strategy also has its perks. The company is vertically integrated and, after spending significant upfront capital on building its rockets, the marginal cost per launch can be lower than what an outside company contracting launch services pays. That's especially true given that SpaceX has pioneered reusable rockets and drastically reduced the cost of space travel.

The company is still innovating. Its next-gen rocket, Starship, is being developed to be fully reusable, with a much bigger payload capacity than its current Falcon 9. Starship could help the company extend its lead over Amazon and other corporations that are looking to enter this market, and SpaceX's lead is already massive. According to some estimates, SpaceX has a little over 11,000 active satellites in orbit. So, it's not time for the company and its shareholders to be worried about Amazon yet.

Which one is a buy?

Amazon doesn't need to dominate the connectivity market to perform well over the medium term. The company's core business, and especially its cloud computing arm, Amazon Web Services (AWS), is booming. In the second quarter, Amazon's sales grew by 20% year over year to $200.6 billion. AWS sales increased by 37% year over year, its fastest growth rate in 18 quarters. On the bottom line, Amazon's earnings per share grew 242% to $5.75 (benefiting from equity investments).

Amazon is seeing significant demand for its cloud and AI services and could ride that wave for a long time, making the stock an attractive pick to hold at least through the next five years. What about SpaceX? Its recent financial performance was strong. Second-quarter revenue grew 92% year over year to $7.8 billion, while the net loss nearly halved to $541 million compared to $1 billion in the year-ago period.

SpaceX could become profitable soon. That's what analysts expect. Even so, the company's shares are very expensive, trading at 208x forward earnings. The business is strong, but at current levels, it may take a while for SpaceX's shares to grow into their valuation. I'd avoid the stock for now.

news.Content:
For a company having a major refounding moment this week, Meta's ( META ) price-to-earnings ratio still looks stuck in the past.

Meta's stock is trading on a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 22 times, below its long-term average of 23.1 times.

The likely reason for the disconnect between Meta's P/E and the bullish week the company's having is that the Street is dragging its feet on raising its 2027 earnings estimates as the company reinvests aggressively in AI infrastructure.

Yahoo Finance data shows next year's earnings estimates on Meta have increased only slightly over the past seven days. Meanwhile, 2027 EPS estimates currently remain well below those seen 90 days ago.

But the EPS trend is poised to change, and investors are betting on that today — Meta stock has surged 14% in the past five days.

Meta's Steve Jobs-like surprise at Meta Connect late Wednesday came in the form of the Muse Charm. It's a standalone pocket device built exclusively for voice interaction with the company's new Muse agent, currently one of the most-downloaded apps.

Zuckerberg also showcased a major shift toward "Personal Superintelligence" by unveiling a hardware-meets-AI moment in the Meta VR Glasses.

Weighing just 100 grams — roughly one-fifth the weight of Meta's Quest 3 — the $1,299 spatial computing glasses feature 5K micro-OLED displays, tethered puck processing, and native eye and hand tracking.

On the smart eyewear front , Meta debuted the third-generation Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3 glasses, starting at an entry-level $249. Joining them are the camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses, designed purely for open-ear listening and AI voice interaction.

Meanwhile, Meta's Muse has amassed more than 3.4 million downloads since its Sept. 8 launch, per new Sensor Tower data obtained by Yahoo Finance.

Muse accumulated 2.8 million downloads in its first two weeks, while competitor AI chatbots, including OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) ChatGPT, SpaceXAI's ( SPCX ) Grok, and Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) Claude, received 3.7 million, 400,000, and 300,000 global downloads, respectively, during the same period (14 days post-launch).

news.Content:
Meta Platforms META is benefiting from its continued push to broaden its virtual reality (VR) portfolio and strengthen the ecosystem around Reality Labs. In the second quarter of 2026, Reality Labs revenues increased 16% year over year to $431 million, driven by Meta Platforms' continued spending on augmented and virtual reality products. The expanding wearable portfolio is strengthening Meta Platforms' positioning against Apple AAPL and Alphabet GOOGL, which are also investing heavily in AI-enabled wearable devices.

Meta Platforms' growing smart-glasses portfolio remains a key catalyst. The company recently unveiled Meta VR Glasses, a roughly 100-gram virtual-reality device designed for entertainment, work and gaming. The glasses feature a 5K Infinite Display with micro-OLED panels, Dolby Vision, and Dolby Atmos, powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon Reality Elite processor. The device integrates Meta AI and supports eye, voice and hand-gesture controls. Meta VR Glasses use a two-part design, with compute, battery and storage housed in a separate tethered puck, helping keep the headset lightweight.

Meta VR Glasses are also the first IMAX Enhanced-certified VR device, offering 3D movies and more than 100 immersive live U.S. sports events annually. The device additionally supports multi-screen workspaces and more than 75 games at launch. Meta VR Glasses will go on sale in spring 2027 for $1,299.99.

However, Meta Platforms' broader VR hardware business remains uneven. Reality Labs' second-quarter growth was partially offset by lower Quest headset sales, even as AI glasses revenues grew strongly. While Reality Labs remains loss-making, the expanding wearable portfolio could provide Meta Platforms with another distribution platform for Meta AI, personal agents and immersive services. The upcoming Meta VR Glasses, scheduled to launch in spring 2027, could further broaden the segment's addressable market across entertainment, gaming and productivity.

How Competitors Fare Against META

news.Title: Serve Robotics Targets a $450B Market: How Big Is Its Growth Runway?
news.Content:
Serve Robotics SERV is pursuing a sizable long-term opportunity as autonomous delivery moves deeper into last-mile logistics. Citing ARK Big Ideas 2025, NHTSA and its own estimates, the company values the robotic and drone delivery market opportunity at $450 billion by 2030. Serve Robotics sees favorable economics in replacing human-courier deliveries that currently cost $8-$10 with robotic delivery potentially costing less than $1 at scale.

The company already has more than 2,000 sidewalk robots, operates across 44 U.S. cities and has completed more than 1.8 million sidewalk and hospital deliveries, with a 99.8% completion rate. Expansion is increasingly focused on improving utilization rather than merely adding robots. DoorDash-derived revenues increased nearly 50% sequentially in the second quarter, while healthcare, advertising and software provide additional growth avenues. Second-quarter revenues climbed 404% year over year to $3.2 million, with recurring revenues accounting for more than half of total sales.

Merchant accessibility could further expand the addressable opportunity. Management estimates that nearly two-thirds of delivery orders in existing markets cannot currently use robotic delivery because of back-of-house integration barriers. Its Beacon product aims to bypass those constraints and connect more restaurants directly to Serve Robotics network.

However, converting the large market opportunity into sustained growth remains challenging. Lower Uber Eats volumes prompted Serve Robotics to slash 2026 revenue guidance to $9-$10 million from $26 million. Therefore, Serve Robotics' runway appears substantial, but execution will depend on raising robot utilization, diversifying demand channels and translating fleet scale into stronger unit economics.

Drone Delivery Rivals Raise the Stakes for Serve

Serve Robotics faces growing competition from Alphabet GOOGL and Amazon AMZN as autonomous delivery expands across the United States. Alphabet's Wing is scaling residential drone delivery with Walmart, targeting a network of more than 270 locations that could reach over 40 million Americans by 2027. Wing has already completed well over one million commercial deliveries, giving Alphabet meaningful operating data and a growing footprint in fast last-mile delivery. Alphabet is also extending Wing into restaurant delivery through partnerships such as Papa Johns.

Amazon is building a competing ecosystem through Prime Air. Amazon plans to expand Prime Air to nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of 2026, offering delivery in as little as 30 minutes across millions of eligible items. Amazon's fulfillment network and logistics scale could accelerate adoption. For Serve Robotics, competition from Wing and Amazon highlights the importance of improving utilization, merchant integration and cost-efficient scaling.

news.Title: The "Magnificent Seven" Stocks: Here's the 1 I'm Buying Hand Over Fist Right Now
news.Content:
The "Magnificent Seven" stocks consist of Nvidia , Apple , Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), Meta Platforms , and Tesla . The term was coined in 2023 when the group drove much of the market's growth.

Their momentum has slowed a bit this year, but they're still seven of the world's 11 most valuable public companies, with Tesla the smallest at a market cap of $1.5 trillion (as of Sept. 22). Each Magnificent Seven stock has a legitimate investing case (I personally own four individually), but the one that stands out as the best investment right now is Google's parent company, Alphabet.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The one-stop AI shop

Over the past few years, the popularity of the Magnificent Seven stocks has revolved around the current AI boom . While some companies rely heavily on third parties, Alphabet's advantage is that it's a vertically integrated AI company with its hand in most parts of the AI ecosystem:

Hardware: Google builds its own advanced AI chips, including the popular Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), which allow it and other companies to train, tune, and deploy AI models.

Google DeepMind: A research arm that focuses on creating safe and responsible AI systems. It's credited with some of the most important AI research over the past decade, helping AI become the powerful tool we interact with today.

Google Cloud: The third-largest cloud platform in the world (behind AWS and Azure), providing critical infrastructure that companies rely on to build, scale, and run their own AI applications.

Gemini: The second-most used AI chatbot, trailing only OpenAI's ChatGPT. It's also the second-fastest-growing chatbot behind Anthropic's Claude.

Alphabet still relies on other companies -- such as Nvidia for GPUs and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing for manufacturing its custom chips -- but much of its AI development happens in-house. This helps reduce costs and lets Alphabet control much of its own destiny, since it isn't reliant on other companies' timelines or pricing models.

The cherry on top is that Alphabet has billions of users across its products and services, enabling it to distribute its AI tools virtually instantly. That combo makes me confident that, regardless of how the current AI arms race plays out, Alphabet will be a long-term winner. AI is a benefit, not critical to its survival.

Story Continues

Google Cloud's momentum is strong

Google Search will always be Alphabet's bread and butter, but Google Cloud is its most promising business right now. I don't foresee it surpassing Amazon's AWS or Microsoft's Azure in market share, but with the overall growth of the cloud industry, third place is still a lucrative position to be in.

news.Content:

Michael Burry ( Trades , Portfolio ) is warning that Big Tech's unprecedented AI infrastructure spending could eventually leave hyperscalers with significant write-offs, arguing that today's buildout is beginning to resemble earlier capital booms that ended with excess capacity and falling returns.

Burry said net capital investment by S&P 500 companies reached 2.07% of U.S. GDP as of June 30, the highest level in nearly four decades outside the aftermath of the March 2000 Nasdaq peak.

I have little doubt the next few quarters will set still higher and higher net investment/GDP marks, possibly even eclipsing that aftermath of the 2000 tech stock peak, Burry wrote.

His concern goes beyond current spending.

Burry estimates Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ), Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ), Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOGL ), Meta Platforms (META) and Oracle ( NYSE:ORCL ) have accumulated roughly $3 trillion in purchase commitments, future leases, guarantees, construction-in-progress and other exposures tied to AI infrastructure.

When the write-offs come, perhaps in 2028 or 2029, these commitments discussed in Part IV may be so large that a relatively small write-off has a bigger impact than we can now imagine, he wrote.

Burry's thesis rests on the capital cycle: heavy investment creates capacity, competition reduces returns, and weaker economics eventually force companies to impair or write down assets.

He pointed to the late-1990s technology, media and telecommunications boom, after which depreciation and write-downs helped push aggregate S&P 500 net investment below zero for 12 consecutive quarters between mid-2003 and mid-2006.

Oracle has become a particular focus of the concern. Burry questioned the company's accounting around customer prepayments and future cloud revenue, while recent anxiety around Oracle's debt and Project Jupiter data center has added to scrutiny of AI infrastructure financing.

Investor takeaway

For investors, Burry's warning is less about whether AI demand exists and more about whether hyperscalers are building infrastructure at returns high enough to justify the commitments.

The critical metrics are free cash flow, capex intensity, utilization, depreciation, lease obligations and returns on invested capital.

If AI revenue continues scaling faster than infrastructure costs, the current spending wave could remain economically rational.

But if utilization, pricing or demand disappoints, even modest asset impairments could have a larger earnings and balance-sheet impact because the commitments are already so large.

That makes 2027 through 2029 especially important for judging whether today's AI buildout becomes a durable productivity cycle or another period of overinvestment.

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Goldman Sachs is turning more cautious on debt issued by the biggest AI hyperscalers as massive infrastructure spending drives a flood of new corporate borrowing. The call is not a rejection of the AI investment thesis, but a warning that relentless bond issuance could pressure valuations across Big Tech credit even if the underlying businesses remain strong.

We believe there will be a lot of hyperscaler issuance, Lindsay Rosner, head of multi-sector fixed income investing at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, told Bloomberg TV. For that sector at large we are underweight knowing more issuance will come.

Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ), Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ), Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOGL ), Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) and Oracle ( NYSE:ORCL ) have been ramping capital spending to finance data centers, chips, power and other AI infrastructure.

That has pushed several Big Tech companies deeper into the corporate bond market.

That is what we have seen all year long, Rosner said. New issuance is replacing existing issuance.

The important distinction is that Goldman's underweight call is primarily about supply.

Rosner said her team still believes in the story of AI, but expects continued borrowing to reprice parts of the credit market as investors absorb larger volumes of new debt.

That matters because the AI buildout is becoming more capital intensive. Hyperscalers have increasingly leaned on debt as free cash flow comes under pressure from enormous capital expenditure programs.

The scale could keep growing. Brookings Institution research cited in the report estimates U.S. AI infrastructure could require roughly $10.3 trillion of investment through 2032, with more financial risk potentially moving away from Big Tech balance sheets and into less-transparent financing structures.

Investor takeaway

For investors, Goldman's warning is more about financing conditions than the long-term AI demand story.

Heavy issuance can push bond spreads wider and raise borrowing costs even when credit quality remains solid.

Investors should watch hyperscaler bond supply, credit spreads, free cash flow, capex intensity and interest expense.

If AI monetization grows quickly enough, today's debt load may remain manageable.

But if borrowing continues faster than cash generation improves, the cost of funding the AI boom could become a larger part of the valuation debate across Big Tech.

news.Title: Chips to Bots: Qualcomm’s Agentic AI Breakout
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Qualcomm Incorporated? Here are five stocks we like better.

Qualcomm is expanding beyond smartphones through new two-nanometer Snapdragon chips and its acquisition of robotics software maker PickNik Robotics to control edge computing.

The company is diversifying into data center optical interconnects and custom chips with Corning and Lumentum to offset expected losses from Apple's baseband modem transition.

Despite a Hold rating and average price target near $204, Qualcomm's dividend, $20 billion buyback program, and strong cash flow limit downside risk for investors.

Wall Street often prices Qualcomm Incorporated (NASDAQ: QCOM) through the lens of cyclical smartphone upgrade patterns, overlooking the transformation unfolding across its product portfolio. By pairing its two-nanometer AI phone chips with the purchase of PickNik Robotics, Qualcomm is systematically establishing control over digital and physical edge computing.

This dual-engine expansion fundamentally resets the growth story as on-device AI scales across consumer and industrial applications.

→ Sandisk Joins the S&P 100—Is the Index Flow, or the AI Story, Driving the Stock?

While 12-month analyst price targets for QCOM average $204, the company's dividend and share buyback spending help limit downside, giving long-term investors an attractive margin of safety during this expansion phase. The market's hesitance to assign QCOM a premium multiple right now presents a distinct opportunity for investors willing to look past immediate handset cycles.

Two-Nanometer Dominance in Premium Smartphones

Qualcomm recently unveiled the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and the higher-spec Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Built on an advanced two-nanometer process node, these chips integrate a custom Oryon CPU, an upgraded Adreno GPU featuring Adreno Neural Fusion, and a specialized Hexagon NPU. The addition of neural fusion bridges the gap between traditional graphics rendering and machine learning tasks, producing smarter graphics that improve battery efficiency and user playtime.

→ Viking's Obesity Edge May Be Staying Power, Not Weight Loss

The core investment thesis revolves around the cost of agentic AI. Market consensus continues to underestimate the cost efficiencies of running AI agents locally on a device. When software developers rely on cloud hyperscalers for AI, they incur recurring token costs and experience latency.

Moving these workloads onto the phone's own chip shifts the compute burden to the device, eliminating those ongoing cloud costs. If Qualcomm edge chips become established as essential infrastructure for real-time digital assistants, the hardware will become a baseline requirement rather than an iterative upgrade.

Story Continues

→ Full Throttle: Kratos and GE Fire Up a Next-Gen Defense Engine

Offering two price tiers for its top chips allows Qualcomm to capture higher average selling prices from major Android manufacturers. Early hardware commitments from global builders like Xiaomi, OnePlus, vivo, and OPPO translate technical leadership into defensible revenue growth. This pricing power helps shield operating margins from memory cost inflation, a headwind currently pressuring handset build schedules across the industry.

Weaponizing the PickNik Acquisition

The mobile segment represents only one side of the edge computing equation. In late September, management announced an agreement to acquire PickNik Robotics, the company that maintains MoveIt, a leading open-source motion-planning framework built on the Robot Operating System.

Securing software-layer control in physical AI provides a distinct structural advantage. By embedding MoveIt directly into its proprietary Dragonwing robotics platform and Arduino VENTUNO Q hardware, Qualcomm builds a foundational developer-ecosystem moat.

This strategy mirrors the developer lock-in that big tech companies successfully built through proprietary compute layers over the last decade. When engineers train and deploy robots using a specific software environment, switching costs become prohibitively high.

Combining industrial automation software with advanced silicon pushes Qualcomm deeper into automated logistics, factory robotics, and physical machinery. Expanding into these industrial sectors creates a large non-handset addressable market that diversifies revenue away from phone upgrade cycles and supports long-term margin stability. Hardware margins naturally stabilize when software integration becomes the primary value driver for the end user.

Optical Interconnects: The New Data Center Catalyst

Beyond phones and robots, Qualcomm is methodically reducing its dependence on a few revenue sources. A recent joint demonstration showcased optical die-to-die interconnects designed for hyperscale systems. Partnering with Corning Incorporated (NYSE: GLW) and Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE), Qualcomm is expanding its total addressable market to include data center interconnect fabrics. As data centers scale to meet AI demand, traditional copper connections face bandwidth bottlenecks, making optical interconnects a necessary evolution for modern compute infrastructure.

Management also confirmed two custom data center chip programs, scheduled to begin generating commercial revenue during the upcoming December quarter. These moves function as an emerging counterweight to expected client losses. The impending loss of baseband modem revenue as Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) transitions to proprietary chips remains a medium-term drag on licensing and chipset volume. Establishing a firm foothold in the data center provides the necessary top-line replacement for Qualcomm.

The Googlebook PC initiative and broader Snapdragon X platform traction offer secondary vectors for high-margin computing market penetration. Taking market share from x86 incumbent chipmakers in the laptop space adds another layer to the revenue diversification strategy, proving Qualcomm can compete effectively outside of mobile architectures.

Pricing the Pivot: Valuation and Strategic Positioning

Qualcomm shares recently bounced out of an acute pullback, recovering from a drop below $178 to trade near $196. At this level, Qualcomm trades at about 22 times trailing earnings and carries a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 25. Qualcomm generates nearly $12 per share in operating cash flow and maintains a return on equity exceeding 38%. With a beta of 1.68, the stock is more volatile than the broader market, which helps explain the recent wide trading range.

Despite strong fundamentals, the current consensus price target sits around $204, implying limited upside. Wall Street rates QCOM a consensus Hold, highlighting reluctance to assign the company a premium valuation without clear top-line acceleration.

This hesitation is partly justified by recent historical performance, as quarterly revenue contracted about 4% year-over-year in the most recent report. Recent insider transactions, including share sales by the CFO, have also contributed to cautious short-term positioning as the market awaits concrete sales data.

Downside risk appears well-protected by aggressive capital allocation measures. A $20 billion share repurchase authorization permits the retirement of nearly 15% of outstanding shares. Combined with an active cash dividend program yielding near 1.8%, these capital returns provide a comfortable margin of safety.

Investors may want to add Qualcomm to their watchlist to monitor whether premium Android pre-orders lift blended chip margins above 21% during the next earnings call. Observing how quickly the custom data center chip scales will provide the clearest signal that this pivot is translating directly into sustained earnings power.

news.Title: Lumentum Shares Are Up After an AI Optical Tech Partnership With Corning and Qualcomm. What This Means for LITE Stock.
news.Content:
Optical networking has become one of the market's hottest AI themes this year. Cloud companies are upgrading their data-center networks and replacing more copper connections with optical ones to handle the huge amounts of data AI systems require. That shift has sent demand higher for companies that make optical components, and many of their stocks have outperformed the broader tech sector.

Lumentum Holdings (LITE) is a clear example. LITE stock has gained 155% this year, well ahead of the 35% rise in the Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLK), and is up 473% over the past 52 weeks.

More News from Barchart

Broadcom Just Named Its Next AI Customer. It Isn't Google.

Dear Microsoft Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for September 24

SpaceX Is Winding Down the Falcon 9. What That Means for SPCX Stock.

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

The latest boost came Monday, when Lumentum announced a joint AI optical-connectivity demonstration with Qualcomm Technologies (QCOM) and Corning (GLW) at ECOC 2026. The companies will show a high-density optical die-to-die, or D2D, system designed for AI scale-up systems. Lumentum shares rose 2.4% in premarket trading after the news, with the stock last trading near $937 and holding an 88% "Buy" rating.

Still, after a gain of more than 465% in a year and with shares near record highs, does this partnership still mark yet another leg of Lumentum's AI growth story? Let's find out.

Inside the Corning-Qualcomm Partnership

Lumentum announced on Sept. 21 that it will demonstrate a high-density optical connection with Qualcomm and Corning at ECOC 2026 in Málaga, Spain. The setup brings together Qualcomm Technologies' chip-to-chip interface technology, Lumentum's 1060-nanometer VCSEL lasers, and Corning's high-density fiber connections.

The demonstration uses 32-gigabit-per-second optical channels and can move about 1 terabit of data per second for every millimeter of chip edge. The companies say the design could eventually reach 4 Tb/s/mm with faster channels and more connections. Lumentum's optical engine can send and receive roughly 10 Tb/s in total. More importantly, the technology can carry data across tens of meters while using less power and producing less delay than traditional electrical links at those distances.

The partnership could put Lumentum's lasers closer to AI chips in future systems that use co-packaged optics and standards such as UCIe. But this is still a demonstration, not a supply deal or a source of near-term revenue. For now, it shows what the three companies can build together and could help draw interest from future customers. Investors liked the news, pushing LITE stock up 2.53% to $954.49 on Sept. 21.

Story Continues

Lumentum's Earnings and Growth Drivers

Lumentum reported a strong fiscal Q4 2026, as demand for its data center products continued to climb. Revenue came in at $1.006 billion, up 109.3% from a year earlier and ahead of Wall Street's $988.6 million estimate. Components revenue rose 102.7% to $649.4 million, while Systems revenue jumped 122.6% to $356.9 million.

Profitability improved, too. Adjusted gross margin rose to 50.4%, operating margin reached 36.6%, and adjusted EPS of $3.23 beat the $2.99 consensus estimate. Lumentum reported a $7.16 billion GAAP loss, but that mostly came from a one-time, noncash $7.8 billion charge related to its convertible notes, not weakness in the underlying business. For fiscal Q1 2027, management expects $1.225 billion to $1.275 billion in revenue and adjusted EPS of $4.05 to $4.35.

Lumentum is also spending to meet future demand. Its 1060-nanometer VCSEL platform, shown at OFC 2026 and used in the project with Qualcomm Technologies Inc. and Corning Inc., is designed for high-speed links between AI chips. The company has shipped more than 10 billion of these laser emitters. It is also building a 240,000-square-foot factory in Greensboro to make advanced indium-phosphide lasers. Nvidia (NVDA) is among its customers. Production is not expected to start until mid-2028, but the expansion shows Lumentum is preparing for sustained demand from large AI data centers.

Wall Street's View on LITE Stock

Lumentum is set to report its next quarterly results on Nov. 3. Wall Street expects the company to earn $3.82 per share for the September quarter, up 536.67% from $0.60 a year ago. For fiscal 2027, analysts expect earnings of $19.78 per share, up 143.30% from $8.13 in fiscal 2026.

Analysts remain bullish after Lumentum Holdings' latest earnings report. J.P. Morgan analyst Joseph Cardoso kept a "Buy" rating and raised his price target to $1,280 from $1,165. Wolfe Research analyst George Notter also kept a "Buy" rating and a $1,200 target. Craig-Hallum analyst Richard Shannon reiterated his "Buy" rating with a $1,150 target, pointing to the company's better-than-expected results and growing data center opportunity.

All 24 analysts tracked rate LITE stock a consensus "Strong Buy." Their average price target is $1,138.12, which suggests 21% upside from current levels.

Conclusion

Lumentum's partnership with Qualcomm and Corning adds another promising layer to its AI story, showing that its VCSEL technology could play a role in the next generation of high-speed connections inside AI systems. Still, this is a technology demonstration, not a revenue-producing contract, so investors should not overstate its near-term financial impact. With earnings accelerating, margins expanding, and capacity investments aimed at AI demand, Lumentum's underlying momentum remains strong. Given its massive run, LITE could see some volatility or profit-taking in the near term, but the shares appear more likely to trend higher over time if management continues converting AI demand into growth.

news.Title: FN Rides on Surging Data Center Demand: Can It Outpace AAOI & LITE?

news.Title: Lumentum Jumped Nearly 10% While Corning Barely Moved. Is the AI Optics Trade Splitting Apart?
news.Content:
When AI stocks rebounded last week, optical networking companies did not rebound equally.

Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: LITE ) jumped nearly 10% in Wednesday trading and led the S&P 500, while Coherent rose 6.9%. Corning Incorporated (NYSE: GLW ) managed only a 0.4% gain and remained down sharply for the week.

All three sit inside the same broad AI-connectivity buildout. The divergence suggests investors are beginning to distinguish between different pieces of that infrastructure rather than buying every optics name together.

Photo from Lumentum Holdings website

Lumentum offers concentrated exposure to the bandwidth problem

AI clusters increasingly need optical connections as more accelerators communicate across larger physical distances. That drives demand for high-speed transceivers, lasers and other photonic components.

For Lumentum Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:LITE), concentrated exposure is both the attraction and the risk. Strong hyperscaler spending can create powerful operating leverage as faster generations of optical links ramp. The same concentration can produce violent corrections when investors question the pace of AI spending or customer deployments.

Corning Incorporated (NYSE:GLW) has a broader business and participates through optical fiber and connectivity infrastructure. The company benefits as hyperscalers build new campuses and connect larger networks, but that exposure is less directly tied to the highest-value transceiver components.

Corning also introduced a fresh complication. A September filing established an equity distribution agreement allowing the company to sell up to $2 billion of stock through Goldman Sachs. That gives Corning capital flexibility for large projects, but potential issuance creates dilution at a moment when investors are already scrutinizing the cost of AI infrastructure expansion.

Professional investors also split on the two names

Insider Monkey's database showed Lumentum ownership falling to 111 hedge funds in Q2 from 123 in Q1. Arrowstreet Capital nevertheless increased its position sharply during the quarter. Corning moved the other way, rising to 99 hedge-fund holders from 91, while Tairen Capital increased its GLW position by roughly 9%.

Lumentum's August 31 short interest stood at about 7.12 million shares, nearly 8% of public float, with approximately 1.7 days to cover. That makes positioning meaningfully heavier than in many large-cap AI infrastructure names.

The takeaway from the rebound is not that Lumentum won and Corning lost. Their economics are different. Lumentum offers more concentrated exposure to high-speed optical components, while Corning offers broader exposure to the fiber-heavy physical buildout underneath them. When the AI trade becomes selective, that distinction suddenly matters.

news.Title: Lumentum to Demonstrate DWDM ELSFP at ECOC 2026: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Lumentum Holdings LITE is benefiting from rising demand for optical connectivity across artificial intelligence (AI) data centers as hyperscalers increasingly shift from copper toward optical links. The company's cloud and AI momentum is being supported by strength across high-power lasers, 200G EMLs, CW lasers, 1.6T transceivers and optical circuit switching. Narrow-linewidth laser assembly shipments increased more than 130% year over year in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, while pump-laser shipments rose more than 80%. Lumentum also expects pump-laser shipments to increase roughly fourfold over the next several quarters.

Building on this momentum, Lumentum announced plans to demonstrate an eight-wavelength DWDM external laser small form factor pluggable (ELSFP) module for Optical Connectivity Interoperability Multi-Source Agreement applications at ECOC 2026. The new module is designed for next-generation co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-packaged optics (NPO) architectures, broadening Lumentum's participation in emerging AI scale-up connectivity. The development complements LITE's existing ultra-high-power laser platform and reinforces its push into external light-source solutions as optical engines move closer to AI accelerators and switches.

The announcement fits Lumentum's broader CPO and NPO strategy. The company expects demand for ultra-high-power laser chips for CPO scale-up connectivity to ramp up in the second half of calendar 2027, ahead of customer deployments in 2028. LITE has received its first external light-source module purchase order for delivery in the second half of 2027. Meanwhile, multiple customers are evaluating NPO as an intermediate step toward CPO, expanding Lumentum's addressable optical market. Its CPO/NPO laser family spans 120-, 150- and 400-milliwatt output levels, supporting both integrated optical engines and external light-source modules.

Lumentum is broadening manufacturing capacity to support growing AI-driven optical demand. The company is expanding capacity across its indium phosphide wafer fabs in Japan to support 200G and 300G lane-speed opportunities. Lumentum began shipping 1.6T transceivers in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, with management expecting adoption to intensify in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and remain strong through calendar 2027. The company is also expanding its U.S. manufacturing footprint, including a new Greensboro, NC, facility that is expected to begin ramping production in mid-2028. These developments strengthen LITE's competitive positioning against Marvell Technology MRVL and Applied Optoelectronics AAOI.

Story Continues

LITE Faces Tough Competition

Marvell is strengthening its position across CPO, NPO, silicon photonics, optical DSPs, TIAs, drivers and switching. Its internally developed NPO light engine and Celestial AI Photonic Fabric broaden its scale-up optics exposure. Marvell noted that NPO is progressing in parallel with CPO, with multiple customers evaluating these architectures. The company is also combining optics with purpose-built scale-up switches, enabling it to offer a more integrated connectivity platform. Management indicated that stronger customer engagement has increased its scale-up optics revenue expectations for fiscal 2028.

AAOI is expanding aggressively in CPO. It plans to ramp ELSFP production through 2027 and targets roughly 400,000 units per month in 2028. The company is expanding in-house laser capacity in Texas and said several customers have already qualified its CPO laser technology. AAOI is also focusing on next-generation DWDM CPO lasers and ELSFP modules. Management expects high-power laser demand to rise materially as CPO adoption broadens, with its vertically integrated laser manufacturing helping support supply, cost control and customer qualification efforts.
